alignments.note: Purpose conjunction realized by the word introducing its English clause.

A universal quantifier with a negator, the ASV writing the negation once as a single 'no'; rule 87 joins the pair, rule 39's test licensing it because the one English word spells the negation and the quantification together, and rule 15 permits the discontinuity. Source head on the quantifier, which occupies the English determiner slot; heading on the negator, or giving 'no' to the negator alone and leaving the quantifier empty, remains defensible.
Modal auxiliary rides with the subjunctive under rule 9; head on the lexical verb.
Subject noun stands bare, the quantifier having taken the determiner slot.
Improper preposition rendered by a single English word, so rule 42's frame question does not arise.
The ASV gives 'God' no determiner, so the article has nothing to anchor and rule 23 empties it; no trailing preposition stands to be moved under rule 101.

review_notes: Rule 87 requires the note to record that the reading is contested; it is recorded on the joined unit.
